issues.body: The P1-2 table says the endpoint has “15/15 in-class scenarios,” but the referenced manifest has 15 executable cases covering only scenarios 2–8 and 11–13; scenarios 1, 9, 10, and 14–16 are out of class. Several scenarios intentionally have multiple cases. Thus 15 is a case count, not a scenario count, and “15/15 scenarios” materially overstates the breadth of conformance behind the recommendation that P1 has substantially landed.
issues.fix_hint: State precisely that 15 executable query-semantics cases pass and identify that they cover 10 of the draft's 16 numbered scenarios, with the remaining 6 delegated out of class. Audit every later “15/15” occurrence and reserve “scenario” for the numbered spec scenarios.
issues.title: AC-SPARQL cases are incorrectly described as 15/15 in-class scenarios

issues.body: Section 5 labels eleven items “future beads” and says none is started, while the repository contract requires future work to be created as beads rather than left as Markdown TODOs. The document also says the stale deviation comment “is captured as a follow-up” without identifying a bead or issue. As written, the proposed milestone has no durable task-graph identity, dependencies, or evidence that the follow-ups were actually captured.
issues.fix_hint: Create beads for the actionable items (deduplicating existing work first), encode the stated dependencies with bd, and replace each plan entry/follow-up assertion with its bead ID. If this document is intentionally only a proposal, remove claims that work is captured and avoid calling the list “future beads” until records exist.
issues.title: The phased plan creates an untracked Markdown backlog

verdict.summary: The reconciliation is well sourced overall, but it contains a material conformance-count overstatement and turns eleven unstarted tasks into a Markdown backlog despite the repository's beads-only tracking rule. Those defects undermine the document's central readiness/sequencing conclusions and must be corrected before approval.
